obligations.text: Offline replay, evaluation, comparison and gate code paths still cannot dispatch a backend: `rustev-eval` has no normal dependency on `rustev-runtime` or `rustev-live`, and only `rustev-live`'s run entry point, reached through `reexecute_live`, may request external work.

No attempt of a live run is sent unless its full worst-case exposure is durably reserved in the persistent journal first and fits both the run cap and the journal's cap; an attempt whose exposure is unknown, whose cost unit is undeclared, or that would pass either cap is refused before any request byte, with its refusal code.

Resumption never re-sends a case whose result was checkpointed and never counts one charge twice: an attempt reserved but not settled before an interruption remains liability in the journal and its case is reported interrupted, re-run only under an explicit flag with new attempt identities.

Every live result is a new run record plus a `rustev.live-reexecution/1` document with `mode` `live_reexecution` and a link to its source case or record; no dataset, bundle, capture, run record, judgment or report used as a source is modified.
Without `rustev eval live`, every existing CLI command, library function, document, golden and plan identity is byte-identical, and the journal file format is unchanged.
An acquisition declared captured is served only from a capture keyed by its request digest; a missing capture is missing evidence for that acquisition and never falls back to a live request.
No dataset case is dispatched until every candidate binding has passed its probe; a failed probe ends the run with `probe_failed` and no case sent.

record.summary: An amendment of approved spec 026 (live re-execution) and of spec 006 (CLI), for #76 child E3 (#74). A new crate `rustev-live` runs a dataset, or the inputs (never the outputs) of retained replay bundles, through one or more candidate plans live, through spec 026's `reexecute_live`, under an explicit `--live` opt-in, a per-run spend cap and the persistent spend journal of spec 012, generalized to any backend with a cost model and moved into `rustev-live`. A runtime spend gate durably reserves every attempt's full worst-case exposure before any byte is sent and refuses an attempt that would pass the run cap or the journal's cap (R-29: USD 5 in total for all testing across providers). Acquisitions are declared live or captured per source; a probe checks reachability and served identity of every candidate binding before any dataset case is sent; scheduling is bounded per binding; runs resume from a checkpoint without re-sending a completed case or counting a charge twice. Every result is new evidence marked `live_reexecution` with a link to its source case or record, and per-run outputs are spec 029 repeat outputs with source `live`, so E1 and E2 consume them unchanged. Approved (A-40); approval authorizes no live run, provider call or spend by itself, raises no cap, and makes no quality claim.
